study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: This study investigated whether personalized brain atrophy maps for individuals with schizophrenia comprised a disorder-specific functional brain network and explained individual variation in clinical response to repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS).

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The software and key preprocessing steps are explicitly mentioned for both structural and functional MRI data.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: Quantitative morphometric analysis was performed using FreeSurfer (version 6.0). In brief, images underwent preprocessing steps including intensity normalization, skull stripping, registration into Talairach space, and determination of the gray-white matter boundary and pial surface. ... Each subject's reconstructed brain was registered to an average spherical template space and smoothed with an 8 mm full width at half maximum kernel.; The rs-fMRI data were preprocessed using SPM12 software (www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/spm) and AFNI (https://afni.nimh.nih.gov/afni/). The processing steps were as follows: (1) delete the first 5 time points, (2) remove temporal spikes more than 2.5 SDs from the mean (AFNI's 3dDespike), (3) slice timing correction, (4) head motion correction, (5) co-registration to the structural image, (6) regress out nuisance regressors (24 head motion parameters, and average signals in the cerebrospinal fluid, white matter, and whole brain), (7) spatial normalization to the MNI space using the matrix produced by structural image segmentation using DARTEL algorithm in SPM12, and (8) spatial smoothing with a 4 mm full width at half maximum Gaussian kernel.

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: W-score (z-score adjusted for age and gender); defined as (expected - actual) / RSD; significant atrophy loci defined as W-score > 2 (corresponding to CT of 2 SDs below mean).
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: The paper explicitly defines the W-score and how it's calculated, and also states the threshold for significant atrophy loci.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: Individual atrophy maps for each patient were defined as CT deviations from normative modeling. ... W-score = (expectedactual)/RSD, where actual is the patient's observed CT, expected is the predicted CT with the application of the nuisance factors and beta weights from the regression in healthy controls (ie, age× β age + gender× β gender ), and RSD is the residual standard deviation (SD) from the GLM. ... We defined the significant atrophy loci of each patient as regions with a W-score > 2, corresponding to a CT of 2 SDs below the mean of healthy subjects.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Pearson's correlations for associations between imaging and symptoms; Linear mixed-effect models for rTMS treatment effect (Time and Group factors, nested within individuals); χ² test for categorical baseline variables; Student's t-test for continuous baseline variables; Spin tests (10,000 permutations) for spatial correlation between brain maps.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Personalized atrophy maps in schizophrenia patients, though heterogeneous, functionally converge to a disorder-specific network and explain individual variation in clinical response to rTMS treatment.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Personalized atrophy maps showed high heterogeneity across patients but functionally converged to a putative schizophrenia network, with 88% maximal overlapping in the bilateral medial prefrontal cortex (MPFC). The connectivity strength of the rTMS target in personalized atrophy networks significantly correlated with PANSS score improvement after active rTMS treatment (r = 0.54, P = .005), but not for sham.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Normative modeling was established using data from a single center, potentially limiting generalizability; the study exclusively focused on schizophrenia patients; findings related to inhibitory rTMS data may not generalize to excitatory rTMS; overlap ratios of personalized atrophy maps and atrophy network maps are not directly comparable due to differences in sparsity.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: Some limitations and future directions should be mentioned. First, the normative modeling was established using data from a single center, and this may not be generalized to other centers. Second, this study exclusively focused on schizophrenia patients. Third, we found that a negative correlation between the rTMS target and atrophy map was associated with poorer symptom improvement. Notably, this result was exclusively based on inhibitory rTMS data. If excitatory rTMS were used, it is possible that the negative correlation of the atrophy map may predict better treatment outcomes. Fourth, we caution that the overlap ratio of the personalized atrophy maps was not comparable to that of the atrophy network maps, because the latter is much less sparse and therefore has higher overlap.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Utilized an 'atrophy network mapping' approach to define personalized atrophy network; employed 'coordinate-based network mapping' to derive schizophrenia network from meta-analysis studies.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The normative model was validated using an additional independent healthy group (n=60) from the same scanner and sequence. The atrophy network was mapped using resting-state functional connectivity MRI from a subgroup of healthy subjects (n=652, a subset of the 797 healthy subjects).
